 Extensive hands-on experience designing, building, and delivering production-grade cloud architectures, preferably on Google Cloud, with relevant AWS or Azure experience also considered.

jobs.title: Director, Fraud Analytics & Risk Management
jobs.description:
At Manulife Bank, protecting our customers, advisors, and business from financial crime is a critical strategic priority. As Director, Fraud Analytics & Risk Management, you will lead the Bank's fraud analytics and intelligence capabilities, leveraging advanced data analytics, customer risk modeling, and fraud technologies to proactively identify, detect, and mitigate fraud across all banking products, channels, and customer journeys.

 This role is responsible for developing a data-driven fraud management ecosystem that delivers strong customer protection while enabling frictionless banking experiences. Working closely with Operations, Risk, Technology, Digital, Data & Analytics, and external partners, you will drive innovative solutions that enhance fraud detection, strengthen customer risk management, and improve fraud prevention outcomes.

 Reporting to the AVP/VP, Fraud Strategy & Operations, you will play a key leadership role in shaping the future state fraud capability at Manulife Bank.

 Position Responsibilities: 
 Lead Fraud Analytics & Intelligence 
 Develop and execute the Bank's fraud analytics strategy across deposits, lending, mortgages, payments, digital banking, contact centre, and advisor channels.
 Establish proactive monitoring and analytical capabilities to detect emerging fraud risks, customer scams, account takeover attacks, identity theft, synthetic identities, mule activity, and organized fraud networks.
 Leverage internal and external data sources to identify fraud trends, vulnerabilities, and opportunities for control enhancement.
 Lead fraud intelligence and root-cause analysis activities to continuously improve detection and prevention effectiveness.
 Build meaningful analytics, dashboards, and executive reporting to support fraud management decision-making.

 Own Customer Risk Scoring & Fraud Decisioning 
 Design, develop, and continuously optimize customer fraud risk scoring models across the customer lifecycle.
 Enhance risk-based authentication, transaction monitoring, and fraud intervention strategies.
 Leverage behavioural analytics, device intelligence, digital signals, transaction patterns, and external intelligence to improve customer risk segmentation.
 Monitor model performance and ensure appropriate governance, oversight, validation, and recalibration.
 Support development of real-time fraud detection and decisioning capabilities as the Bank evolves its payments and digital banking ecosystem.

 Advance Fraud Technology Capabilities 
 Lead evaluation, implementation, and optimization of fraud technology solutions that strengthen the Bank's fraud prevention capabilities.
 Partner with vendors to implement prevention and detection fraud toolkits
 Develop business cases and strategic recommendations for fraud technology investments.
 Manage vendor relationships, performance expectations, and ongoing solution effectiveness reviews.

 Strengthen Fraud Risk Management 
 Lead comprehensive fraud risk assessments across products, processes, channels, and strategic initiatives.
 Partner with Enterprise Risk Management and Compliance teams to ensure fraud risks are appropriately identified, measured, monitored, and mitigated.
 Define and maintain fraud risk indicators, thresholds, risk appetite metrics, and reporting frameworks.
 Identify control gaps and drive remediation strategies.
 Support regulatory, audit, and governance reviews related to fraud risk management.

 Enable Data-Driven Fraud Prevention 
 Partner with Analytics on developing predictive models to improve fraud detection and prevention outcomes.
 Leverage machine learning, network analytics, behavioural analytics, anomaly detection, and AI-enabled capabilities where appropriate.
 Balance fraud loss reduction objectives with customer experience considerations.
 Translate complex analytical findings into actionable business recommendations for senior leadership.

 Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team 
 Build and lead a team of fraud analytics, fraud intelligence, and risk professionals.
 Foster a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, accountability, and customer focus.
 Coach and develop talent while building future fraud analytics capabilities for the Bank.
 Serve as a trusted advisor to executives and stakeholders on fraud risk trends, emerging threats, and mitigation strategies.

 Required Qualifications: 
 University degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Business, Finance, Risk Management, or a related discipline.
 10+ years of experience in fraud analytics, fraud risk management, financial crimes, banking analytics, or advanced data analytics. 
 Deep understanding of fraud risks across retail banking products and customer journeys.
 Experience developing fraud detection models, customer risk scoring frameworks, and fraud monitoring programs.
 Experience managing fraud technology vendors and implementing fraud 

 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills. 
 Graduate degree in a quantitative or business discipline. Professional certifications such as: Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) 
 Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS) 
 Certified Analytics Professional (CAP) 

 Experience with machine learning and AI-enabled fraud detection solutions. 
 Experience supporting real-time payments, digital banking, and emerging payment ecosystems.
 Experience working with SQL, Python, SAS, Power BI, Tableau, machine learning and predictive analytics tools, fraud detection and case management platforms, identity verification technologies, behavioural analytics solutions, and device intelligence platforms to support data-driven decision-making, fraud prevention, and operational effectiveness.

 Success in This Role 
 You will be successful if you:
 Demonstrate strategic thinking and strong business acumen.
 Drive measurable improvements in fraud control effectiveness.
 Proactively identify emerging fraud risks before they impact customers.
 Build strong partnerships across the Bank and Enterprise.
 Translate complex fraud risks into actionable business recommendations.
 Balance customer experience, operational efficiency, regulatory requirements, and risk management objectives

jobs.title: AVP, GTO Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
As AVP, GTO Strategy & Transformation, you will lead GTO's strategy, transformation agenda, and multi-year roadmap, while also overseeing the GTO global AI platform roadmap. Your focus will be on shaping where GTO is going and ensuring its transformation delivers measurable business value. You will lead multi-year strategy development, operating model transformation, AI enablement, value realization, workforce modernization, and enterprise-scale transformation initiatives. Working closely with Technology, Operations, Finance, People Partners, and business leaders, you will identify opportunities to redesign how work gets done, convert productivity gains into measurable business outcomes, and help build an AI-enabled growth engine that supports growth while maintaining expense discipline. This is an AI-native team — the team uses AI tools, agentic workflows, and LLM-connected platforms as its primary way of working, not as an occasional add-on. 

 Position Responsibilities: 
 GTO Strategy & Strategic Planning: Lead development of multi-year GTO strategy, transformation roadmaps, investment priorities, and strategic planning processes. Translate enterprise objectives into executable plans across Technology and Operations, ensuring strategic intent is reflected in investment and delivery decisions before resources are committed.
 AI-Native Operating Model Transformation: Design and evolve future-state operating models that combine AI, automation, workforce transformation, and technology productivity to sustainably improve capacity, customer outcomes, and efficiency across Technology and Operations — including delivery models, product operating models, workforce structures, and technology ways of working.
 Technology Productivity Realization: Partner with CIOs, COOs, and segment leaders to identify, quantify, and realize value from technology productivity improvements — including product operating models, engineering productivity, and delivery modernization — ensuring productivity gains translate into measurable operational and business outcomes rather than remaining theoretical.
 Operational Transformation & Value Realization: Lead enterprise operational transformation initiatives across customer service, operations, digital channels, workforce productivity, and support functions. Current focus areas may include contact centre transformation, containment optimization, service modernization, and AI-enabled efficiency programs — with the underlying methodology (diagnostic rigor, cross-source data reconciliation, quantified business cases) designed to generalize to future transformation priorities as GTO's agenda evolves.
 Workforce Transformation & Future Skills: Define workforce transition strategies, future-skill requirements, role redesign opportunities, and redeployment approaches required to support AI-enabled operating models. Partner with People Partners, L&D, and segment leaders to drive execution — setting direction, tracking progress, and identifying opportunities to accelerate adoption in partnership with segment leaders.
 Enterprise Value Realization: Own benefit targets and KPI commitments across the GTO transformation portfolio. Establish and govern enterprise value realization methodologies, validate assumptions, reconcile benefit calculations across data sources, create defensible performance baselines, and ensure reported outcomes remain transparent and defensible to senior leadership and ELT — explicitly separating transformation-driven impact from organic or external trends.
 Product & Portfolio Leadership Strengthened: Own and evolve the GTO AI product roadmap, defining priorities and sequencing releases across initiatives and reusable capabilities. Ensure product investments align with GTO strategic priorities and target-state operating model objectives, rather than being pursued independently of the broader transformation agenda.
 Executive & Board-Level Narrative Ownership: Own the preparation of ELT and Board/Technology Committee-ready materials — portfolio checkpoints, anticipated-Q&A briefs, and strategic narratives — translating complex, multi-segment operational and financial data into clear, decision-ready formats. Anticipate scrutiny across every segment and function represented, not just the primary owner's area, and ensure diplomatic, precise, and defensible framing throughout.
 GTO Global AI Platform Roadmap Ownership: Own and oversee the GTO global AI platform roadmap — set the AI direction and transformation agenda for GTO across 14 countries, translate enterprise AI vision into operational priorities, and ensure the platform roadmap is directly sequenced against GTO's broader multi-year strategy and transformation agenda rather than developed in isolation. Apply strategic rigour to problem framing and solution design, ensuring the right problems are prioritized before delivery resources are committed, and assess strategic AI hypotheses through structured pilots prior to scaling investment.
 Outcome Measurement: Establish clear success measures — adoption, operational impact, cycle-time improvements, reliability — and report progress to senior leadership.
 Delivery Execution: Lead end-to-end delivery planning and execution for approved transformation and AI initiatives, ensuring predictable release rhythms and timely removal of blockers.
 Competitive Intelligence: Maintain ongoing awareness of AI and transformation developments across financial services and the broader enterprise landscape. Translate external signals — competitor moves, emerging capabilities, regulatory shifts — into strategic implications for the GTO agenda.
 Production Readiness: Drive readiness reviews with Technology, Enterprise AI, and Risk partners to confirm controls, documentation, and deployment plans are in place prior to release.
 Cross-functional Escalation: Act as escalation point for delivery throughput issues, coordinating cross-functional resolution and trade-off decisions.
 Platform Reuse & Scaling: Lead the shift from project-by-project delivery to a reusable capability model — shared components, templates, evaluation patterns, and connectors.
 Governance Alignment: Ensure solutions align with Responsible AI and model risk expectations, including appropriate documentation and monitoring plans.
 Opportunity Identification & Prioritization: Identify, quantify, and prioritize AI and operational-transformation opportunities across GTO using structured analysis and operational input — including digital-capability heatmapping, deflection/containment sizing, and repeat-contact root-cause analysis. Build data-driven business cases with Finance and Operations leaders, using the same rigor applied to product investment decisions.
 Transformation Investment Prioritization: Evaluate strategic initiatives, validate business cases, recommend investment priorities, and support trade-off decisions across the GTO portfolio.
 Executive Decision Support & Strategic Communications: Serve as a primary architect of executive decision support across GTO — ELT materials, Board and Technology Committee narratives, investor-facing content, anticipated-Q&A preparation, and strategic storyline development. Treat this as a defining capability of the function, not a byproduct of other work: the quality of this synthesis directly shapes how senior leadership and the Board understand GTO's transformation progress.
 AI-First Operating Model: Lead by example in how the team works. Personally use LLM-connected agents, enterprise agentic AI platforms, and AI-augmented workflows to reimagine how portfolio reporting, strategy synthesis, operational diagnostics, and executive communications are produced — including live querying of enterprise data platforms to validate findings in real time. Set the standard for the team and demonstrate that AI-first ways of working are operational — not aspirational.
 People Leadership: Build and lead a high-performing team focused on operational discipline, delivery excellence, and continuous improvement.

 Required Qualifications: 
 Experience leading enterprise strategy, operating model redesign, or large-scale transformation efforts across Technology, Operations, or shared services environments.
 10+ years of experience in strategy, transformation leadership, product leadership, technology delivery, platform programs, and/or AI-enabled transformation, preferably in regulated industries.
 Proven track record delivering complex products, transformation programs, or platforms into production with measurable outcomes, including release planning and dependency management.
 Experience operating at enterprise scale across multiple geographies or business units, including setting targets and holding accountability for benefit realization.
 Demonstrated experience in operational analytics — diagnosing performance issues from raw operational data, reconciling discrepancies across data sources, and translating findings into funded business cases.
 Strong ability to lead cross-functionally in matrixed environments and communicate clearly with senior stakeholders.
 Strong experience in quantitative modeling, scenario analysis, and business case development.
 Working knowledge of modern AI solution patterns (e.g., LLM-enabled assistants, intelligent document processing, agent-based workflows) and production readiness considerations.
 Hands-on orientation with AI productivity tools and agentic workflows; personally comfortable using LLM-connected enterprise tools — including direct querying of enterprise data platforms — to accelerate strategy, reporting, and synthesis work.
 Experience working with executive leadership teams, Boards, Technology Committees, or governance forums to support strategic decision-making.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience evolving operating models from project-based to product/platform delivery.
 Familiarity with MLOps/LLMOps concepts, evaluation approaches, monitoring, and model governance practices.
 Experience influencing people strategy, workforce transformation, or AI reskilling programs in a tech/operations context.
 Demonstrated ability to validate strategic hypotheses through pilots and translate early wins into enterprise momentum.
 Experience with contact centre or operations analytics — IVR/self-service containment, FCR/repeat-contact analysis, workforce management metrics — in a multi-country or multi-segment environment.
 Advanced degree or equivalent experience in engineering, computer science, data science, or business.

jobs.title: AVP, Enterprise Digital Capabilities
jobs.description:
We are seeking a strategic, collaborative and product-minded leader to join our team as Assistant Vice President (AVP), Enterprise Digital Capabilities. This role is a key leader in Manulife's multi-year transformation to modernize and converge our digital ecosystem across Canada, the US, Asia and Global Wealth & Asset Management.

At the heart of this role is a simple objective: identify what is common across our digital experiences, build it once as an enterprise capability, and enable markets and segments to reuse and extend it to accelerate their own digital roadmaps.

Manulife has established a strong portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities that support our Digital Storefront transformation and broader unification ambitions. The next opportunity is to expand and scale this portfolio to accelerate the unification strategies and roadmaps of our segments and advance One Manulife experiences across the enterprise. The AVP will lead this evolution – working across segments to identify where common capabilities can create the greatest incremental value, bringing together requirements to ensure capabilities are designed for enterprise reuse, defining adoption and rollout strategies, and establishing a federated model where capabilities can be developed globally or contributed by segments and scaled for broader enterprise benefit.

The AVP will own the strategy and evolution of this portfolio — identifying new opportunities for reuse, prioritizing investment, establishing strong product management disciplines, driving adoption, optimizing existing capabilities and ensuring that each enterprise investment continues to deliver measurable value.

A critical part of the role is leading the Common Capability Collective, bringing together digital and product leaders from across the enterprise to identify common needs, align roadmaps, determine where enterprise investment can eliminate duplication and accelerate delivery, and create a shared view of capability priorities.

This is an enablement role, not ownership of individual market or segment experiences. The AVP will partner closely with Digital Storefront and segment digital leaders to understand their roadmaps and determine how enterprise capabilities can help them deliver faster, with greater quality, consistency and efficiency.

The AVP will operate in a two-in-a-box partnership with a complementary Global Technology leader, jointly shaping the business and technology evolution of enterprise digital capabilities. Together, they will ensure capabilities are scalable, secure, reusable, well-integrated and designed for long-term enterprise value.

 Position Responsibilities 

 Enterprise Capability Strategy & Portfolio 

 Own the strategy, roadmap and ongoing evolution of Manulife's portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities.
 Establish a clear view of the capabilities required to support digital convergence across markets, segments and channels.
 Continuously identify common business and customer needs that can be solved once and reused across the enterprise.
 Assess existing segment capabilities for opportunities to scale them globally rather than rebuilding equivalent solutions.
 Prioritize enterprise investment based on customer value, segment demand, reuse potential, strategic alignment and economic benefit.
 Maintain a multi-year capability roadmap aligned to Digital Storefront, segment roadmaps and Manulife's broader digital strategy.
 Ensure the portfolio remains focused and sustainable by rationalizing overlapping capabilities, technology and licenses where appropriate.

 Common Capability Collective & Federated Leadership 

 Lead the Common Capability Collective, bringing together Digital Storefront and product leaders from across the enterprise to jointly shape capability priorities and investment.
 Create transparency across segment roadmaps to identify shared needs, opportunities for reuse and potential duplication before investment occurs.
 Establish a federated model that enables capabilities to originate within segments where appropriate and subsequently evolve into reusable enterprise capabilities.
 Build alignment around enterprise standards and shared capabilities while preserving segment accountability for their own customer experiences and business outcomes.
 Create clear decision rights, funding principles, ownership models and governance for the creation and evolution of common capabilities.

 Product Management & Capability Evolution 

 Establish strong product management disciplines across the enterprise capability portfolio, including product vision, roadmaps, adoption, performance measurement and lifecycle management.
 Ensure every capability has clear customer and business outcomes, ownership, success measures and an evolution roadmap.
 Use segment feedback, performance data and emerging customer needs to continuously improve capabilities.
 Drive adoption and reuse across markets and segments, ensuring enterprise investments translate into meaningful acceleration of local roadmaps.
 Ensure capabilities are designed for extensibility so segments can meet differentiated market needs without unnecessarily duplicating core functionality.
 Manage capabilities through their full lifecycle, including investment, enhancement, optimization, consolidation and retirement.

 AI Enablement & Optimization 

 Establish an AI-by-default approach to the development and evolution of enterprise digital capabilities.
 Identify opportunities to embed AI directly into capabilities to improve customer experiences, decisioning, personalization and digital effectiveness.
 Apply AI and automation across the capability lifecycle to accelerate development, testing, implementation, operations and ongoing optimization.
 Partner with Technology and enterprise AI teams to identify emerging AI capabilities that can be productized and reused across the organization.
 Continuously evaluate opportunities to reduce manual effort, improve quality and accelerate time to market through AI-enabled capabilities and ways of working.

 Enterprise Integration & Technology Partnership 

 Co-lead the enterprise capability portfolio in close partnership with Global Technology through a two-in-a-box leadership model.
 Define business requirements and product priorities while partnering with Technology on architecture, engineering, security, scalability and technical lifecycle management.
 Ensure enterprise capabilities are designed to integrate effectively across Manulife's digital ecosystem and can be consumed by multiple platforms, markets and channels.
 Promote API-enabled, modular and reusable approaches that reduce point-to-point solutions and technology duplication.
 Ensure platform and technology decisions support long-term reuse, interoperability and enterprise scale.

 Business Value & Benefits Realization 

 Establish a clear value proposition and business case for enterprise digital capabilities and the overall portfolio.
 Quantify and track the value generated through reuse, including delivery acceleration, avoided duplicate investment, license consolidation, operational efficiency, improved customer experience and reduced ongoing support costs.
 Demonstrate how building once and reusing at scale compounds speed, quality and efficiency with every additional implementation.
 Partner with Global Marketing Strategy, FP&A, Technology and segment teams to track expected and realized benefits.
 Use adoption, utilization, performance and financial data to inform ongoing investment and portfolio decisions.

 Adoption & Enterprise Enablement 

 Partner with segment digital leaders to understand upcoming priorities and proactively identify enterprise capabilities that can accelerate their roadmaps.
 Establish clear onboarding, documentation, implementation patterns and support models that make enterprise capabilities easy for teams to adopt.
 Build awareness and understanding of available capabilities across the organization to increase reuse and prevent unnecessary reinvention.
 Create feedback loops with consuming teams so capabilities continue to evolve based on real implementation and customer needs.
 Champion a culture of reuse and enterprise thinking while recognizing the differentiated needs of individual markets and businesses.

 Required Qualifications 

 Bachelor's degree in Business, Digital, Technology, Marketing or a related discipline; MBA or master's degree preferred.
 10+ years of experience in digital product management, digital transformation, enterprise capabilities, platforms or related leadership roles.
 Demonstrated experience building and scaling reusable digital products, platforms or capabilities across a complex, federated organization.
 Strong understanding of modern digital ecosystems, including APIs, cloud platforms, identity, personalization, search, content, data, analytics, experimentation and customer experience technologies.
 Experience establishing product management disciplines and managing a portfolio of digital products or capabilities through their lifecycle.

jobs.description:

 The Director will lead and manage a team, providing clear direction, oversight, and ongoing development, while ensuring procurement-related third-party risk activities are executed in line with internal policies, audit expectations, and regulatory requirements.

 The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in audit, regulatory compliance, and Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and will serve as a key point of contact for regulators (e.g., OSFI), Internal Audit, and Second Line Risk. This role requires a strong, confident leader with a strategic and critical mindset, capable of influencing stakeholders, challenging constructively, and delivering consistent, high-quality outcomes.

 Contracts executed prior to completion of required risk assessments

 Ensure all outputs are accurate, consistent, evidence-based, and defensible

 Policy, Guidelines & Advisory 
 Develop and maintain TPRM guidelines, processes, and playbooks aligned to regulatory expectations

 Provide guidance to business units on:
 Handling supplier confidential documentation requests

 Application of TPRM requirements in complex or non-standard scenarios (e.g., exceptions, travel-related vendors)

 Leadership & Strategic Direction 
 Lead, manage, and develop a high-performing team, providing clear direction, priorities, and performance expectations

 Set and execute a strategic vision for Quality Assurance and TPRM governance

 Foster a culture of accountability, integrity, and continuous improvement

 Build team capability through training, coaching, and ongoing development

 Partner with senior stakeholders across Procurement, Risk, and Business Units to influence outcomes and strengthen risk management practices

 10+ years of experience in Third Party Risk Management (TPRM), Operational Risk, Audit, or Compliance

 Deep expertise in:
 Audit practices and regulatory expectations

 RCSA frameworks, control design, and risk assessment methodologies

jobs.title: Director, Global Technology & Operations Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
The Director, Global Technology & Operations Strategy & Transformation will help shape and execute strategic priorities across Global Technology & Operations (GTO), with a significant focus on leading the AI program and translating strategy into measurable business outcomes.

 The Director will lead the AI program across GTO, bringing together strategy, business case development, funding, program governance, technical delivery, adoption, and value realization. This includes managing AI program funding, ensuring funding is directed to the appropriate initiatives and teams, and maintaining visibility into how initiatives are progressing against delivery commitments, defined success criteria, and approved budgets.

 Working closely with the VP of GTO and senior stakeholders across Business, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, and Risk, the Director will provide an integrated view of the AI program, drive accountability across teams, identify areas requiring leadership attention, and enable informed decisions on priorities, funding, execution, and outcomes.

 The Director will also help shape how GTO delivers its AI agenda, establishing approaches to prioritize and sequence initiatives, accelerate execution, and scale reusable AI capabilities across segments and countries. This includes helping establish a practical path from opportunity identification through development, production, and adoption, while focusing resources on initiatives that can deliver the greatest strategic and business impact.

 Position Responsibilities
 GTO Strategy & Transformation: Partner with the VP of GTO and senior leaders to translate strategic priorities into executable strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, and measurable outcomes. Connect priorities across teams, identify opportunities and risks, and provide insights and recommendations to support executive decision-making.
 AI Program Leadership & Governance: Lead the end-to-end AI and Automation program across GTO, establishing a single integrated view of initiatives, priorities, dependencies, funding, and outcomes. Establish program governance and operating rhythms and work across Product Owners, Segment Leads, Technology, and business and functional partners to drive execution, alignment, and accountability.
 AI Strategy, Prioritization & Delivery Approach: Help define how GTO identifies, assesses, prioritizes, sequences, and delivers AI initiatives. Develop practical prioritization and delivery approaches that consider strategic alignment, business value, delivery readiness, scalability, complexity, funding requirements, dependencies, and risk. Continuously assess the portfolio to ensure resources remain focused on the highest-value opportunities and identify where initiatives should be accelerated, repositioned, or deprioritized.
 Business Case & AI Program Funding: Lead the planning, mobilization, and partner engagement required to develop business cases for AI execution and future funding, including cost-benefit analysis, expected outcomes, success criteria, delivery requirements, and risk considerations. Manage AI program funding and recommend allocation or reallocation across initiatives and teams based on strategic priorities, expected value, delivery readiness, and performance.
 Delivery Excellence, Performance & Value Realization: Oversee AI initiatives across technical delivery, business outcomes, adoption, success criteria, budget utilization, risks, and dependencies. Assess whether initiatives are delivering against their original commitments, drive accountability for results, and identify where intervention, reprioritization, or funding adjustments are required. Ensure realized outcomes can be traced back to approved business cases and defined success measures.
 Executive Reporting & Stakeholder Management: Provide the VP of GTO and senior leadership with a consolidated view of the AI program, including roadmap progress, funding utilization, delivery performance, value realization, risks, dependencies, and decisions required. Maintain effective engagement across sponsors, segments, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, Risk, and other partners, translating complex information into clear executive insights and recommendations.
 AI-Driven Transformation & Reusable Capabilities: Identify opportunities to fundamentally redesign processes and ways of working through AI and Automation, moving beyond incremental improvements. Drive the development, reuse, and adoption of scalable AI capabilities, standards, playbooks, and common approaches that accelerate delivery and reduce duplication across GTO.

 Required Qualifications
 8+ years of experience across strategy and transformation, technology, AI, program management, product management, or related disciplines, with demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional programs.
 Demonstrated experience leading large-scale AI, Automation, technology, innovation, or transformation programs, including program governance, prioritization, funding, delivery oversight, and performance management.
 Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with demonstrated experience translating strategy into prioritized programs, roadmaps, business cases, funding recommendations, and measurable outcomes.
 Strong financial acumen, including experience developing and evaluating business cases, cost-benefit analysis, managing budgets and funding, establishing success measures, and assessing value realization.
 Strong understanding of AI platforms and modern AI solution patterns, with sufficient technical fluency to understand delivery plans, challenge assumptions, assess dependencies and risks, and engage credibly with Technology and AI leaders.
 Strong program leadership capabilities, including the ability to oversee multiple concurrent initiatives, establish governance and delivery frameworks, manage complex dependencies, and drive disciplined execution across Business and Technology teams.
 Exceptional executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to synthesize complex strategic, financial, business, and technical information into clear insights, recommendations, and decisions for senior leadership.
 Demonstrated ability to influence and challenge senior stakeholders, drive accountability without direct authority, create structure in ambiguous environments, and manage competing strategic priorities.
 Demonstrated use of AI productivity tools and agentic workflows to accelerate analysis, synthesis, reporting, decision-making, and content development.

 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience leading or managing an enterprise-scale AI, Automation, technology, innovation, or transformation program, including prioritization, funding, delivery, and value realization.
 Experience establishing program governance, portfolio prioritization frameworks, business cases, executive reporting, and value-realization models.
 Familiarity with enterprise AI architecture, MLOps/LLMOps, AI evaluation, Responsible AI, model governance, and the considerations involved in moving AI solutions from development into production.
 Experience scaling reusable AI capabilities across multiple teams, business segments, or geographies.
 Experience partnering directly with senior executives on strategy, funding, program performance, prioritization, and enterprise transformation.
 Financial services or other highly regulated industry experience strongly preferred.

jobs.title: Vice President, Group Functions Technology - Finance & Treasury Systems
jobs.description:
The VP Group Functions Technology (GFT) Finance Systems is accountable for formulating and driving global information services, technology strategies, management, and implementations for Manulife Group Finance (GF) as well as day to day operations for our finance and treasury portfolios. This role is the Information Services lead for the Finance and Treasury and has a clear mandate to identify opportunities to utilize technology to maximize productivity as well as efficiencies while supporting the evolving needs of the business and their clients across Canada, the United States, Japan, Hong Kong and the rest of Asia.  This includes developing the IS application strategy and overseeing its execution to meet goals within agreed targets and budget for GFT Finance Systems. 

 This role is accountable for effectively leading and managing large and complex IS application integrations and the coordination of technical infrastructure projects, ensuring that the communication of requirements and expectations are clear and projects are completed on time and deployed in a controlled and user inclusive manner across the enterprise globally. 

 This role will require a deep understanding of both financial processes and cash management best practices, as well as the ability to drive operational excellence and delivery efficiency.  This role has accountability directly to the SVP & CIO of Group Functions Technology and to provide services to the heads of the various Group Finance Functions and their teams including the VP, Chief Accountant as well the SVP & Treasurer.  

 Position Responsibilities: 

 Individual Accountabilities: 

 Partner with the functions and provide thought leadership, develop and provide authoritative advice related to emerging and innovative solutions. 
 Develop a service oriented team and culture across GFT and collaborate with cross-functional teams to define and prioritize technology requirements for finance and treasury initiatives. 
 Operate within budget targets to add value while ensuring business goals are met. 
 Oversee all technology roles, services, budgets and savings within GFT and manage the relative spend ratio between build and run. 
 Implement technology vision and operating model within GFT. 
 Drive operational excellence and continuous improvement in service management to effectively achieve associated SLA’s and SLO’s and enable the success of the technology strategy for business units throughout the enterprise. 
 Maintain and adhere to governance for Sox compliance, regulators, internal and external auditors as well as all key risk and control standards for Information Risk Management. 
 Execute technology talent strategy and headcount planning across the areas of accountability and the selection, retention and development of senior level professional staff for the GFT group, across Canada and global operating area. 

 Key Shared Accountabilities: 

 Leveraging technology to optimize efficiencies and standardized business processes.  
 In conjunction with the Global Enterprise Architecture & Engineering Office, develop appropriate application architecture standards for Group Functions and enforce adherence.  
 With a focus on key vendors, leverage global practices for the execution of vendor management strategy in coordination with Procurement and vendor management policies.  
 Active participation and input into appropriate Business Continuity Planning, Disaster Recovery, Information Risk and Security globally for GFT.                                                                                                            

 Required Qualifications: 

 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field. 
 Finance Technology / General Ledger experience is mandatory. 
 15+ years of increasing responsibility in strategy, process or technology oriented areas with deep and broad knowledge of financial services and the insurance industry. 
 Strong understanding of financial and cash management frameworks, regulations, and industry standards. 
 Ability to manage multiple high profile conflicting priorities typically found in a large and complex project portfolio that spans multiple business lines, ensuring deliveries are on time and budget. 
 International exposure and ability to work with a variety of cultures and perspectives.  Senior professional with extensive experience developing and integrating complex services and systems.  
 Strategic thinker, thinks conceptually beyond day-to-day business realities, creates a clear vision for the business and adopts a long-term perspective.  
 First-hand experience in management of unexpected crisis and ensures timely resolution. 
 Ability to engage and influence at all levels of the organization.  Interacts in ways that gain acceptance and commitment, influence opinion and resolve conflicts. 
 Proven interpersonal skills: two-way communications skills (oral and written), ability to build relationships, influence others, work with a diverse internal and international customer base. 
 Solid track record of delivering innovative sustainable technology solutions, reducing costs, increasing productivity. 
 Able to function as an organizational change agent and see beyond current situations towards enterprise-wide higher level process and systems improvements and reengineering departments through leadership, and innovation. 
 Strong services and systems aptitude; demonstrated project management and planning skills; balances strategic skills with tactical execution skills. 
 Strong operations efficiency orientation (process, costing, etc.) and ability to effectively manage ongoing operations within budget targets while identifying opportunities for ongoing efficiency.

McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

 We are seeking an exceptional Director, Data Platforms & Analytics Technology to join McKesson Technology US Pharmaceutical Distribution (USPD) Decision Intelligence organization and lead the execution of design, development, and optimization of USPD data products. This role involves setting the technical vision, managing high-performing teams, and aligning data strategy with business objectives while managing large-scale data products built on modern data stack. This role involves collaborating with stakeholders to align data capabilities with business objectives and overseeing data governance, security, and best practices.  The successful candidate will combine deep technical expertise with proven leadership capabilities to deliver high-impact data solutions that power critical business decisions across our USPD portfolio.

 Key Accountabilities: 
 Strategic Leadership 
 Partner with executives, business leaders, and technology stakeholders to define data architecture vision and roadmap
 Drive innovation in data engineering practices, emerging technologies, and platform capabilities to maintain competitive advantage
 Establish data engineering standards, best practices, and governance frameworks across the organization
 Technical Excellence 
 Design, build, and maintain scalable and AI-ready data products leveraging Microsoft Azure ecosystem, ensuring efficient data ingestion, transformation, and storage. 
 Lead advanced implementation of Databricks for large-scale data processing, machine learning workflows, and real-time analytics
 Organizational Leadership 
 Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team of Data Engineering Directors, and technical specialists
 Collaborate cross-functionally with Operations, Data Science, Analytics, IT, and Business Intelligence teams to deliver integrated solutions
 Establish talent development programs, technical career progression paths, and engineering excellence initiatives
 Foster culture of innovation, continuous learning, and technical excellence within the data engineering organization
 Operational Excellence

 Implement comprehensive monitoring, alerting, and incident response capabilities for mission-critical data systems
 Partner with Enterprise Data Platform team to implement automation and AI accelerator initiatives, and DevOps practices to enhance deployment speed and operational reliability
 Manage technology budgets, vendor relationships, and strategic partnerships to optimize total cost of ownership

 Ensure data platform security, compliance, and performance optimization across all environments

 12+ years experience of professional experience in related IT field with 4+ years experience in leadership, planning and communication roles.

 Critical Skills 
 Deep expertise in Microsoft Azure data services ecosystem (Azure Data Factory, Synapse Analytics, Data Lake Storage, Event Hubs, Cosmos DB)
 Advanced proficiency with Databricks platform and advanced analytics workflows
 Extensive experience with BI development, administration, and enterprise deployment
 Strong foundation in modern data architectures, scalable Lakehouse using Medallion patterns and Unity Catalog; "RAG-ready" infrastructures and AI-driven data observability to automate quality and drift detection, real-time streaming, and event-driven systems
 Proficiency in multiple programming languages (Python, Scala, SQL,.NET) and infrastructure

 Additional Experience 
 Strong technical aptitude and experience with a wide variety of technologies 
 Ability to rapidly learn and if required evaluate a new tool or technology 
 Strong verbal & written communication skills 
 Demonstrated technical leadership experience 
 Be an innovative thinker 
 Must have a strong customer and quality focus 
 Have been successful in working across organizational boundaries, bringing together people with diverse perspectives and experience to find solutions to complex technical issues 
 Proven experience in architecting AI-First Data Platforms, leveraging Generative AI to automate data curation workflows and implementing RAG-ready architectures that serve both structured BI and unstructured LLM applications.
 Azure certifications (Azure Data Engineer Associate, Azure Solutions Architect Expert)
 Databricks certifications (Professional Data Engineer, Professional ML Practitioner)
 Experience in regulated industries (healthcare, financial services, manufacturing)

 Master’s. Degree in Computer Science, Engineering or equivalent.

 Directeur(trice) principal(e) de l’architecture de solutions/Senior Director, Solution Architecture

 À propos du poste

 McKesson recherche un(e) Directeur(trice) Principal(e), Architecture d’Entreprise et Expérience Numérique pour diriger la stratégie d’architecture couvrant l’architecture de solutions, l’architecture applicative, la modernisation des solutions héritées (legacy) et la gestion de l’expérience numérique. Ce leader définira la vision de solutions technologiques modernes, évolutives, sécurisées et centrées sur le client afin de soutenir les priorités de l’entreprise et d’améliorer les résultats opérationnels.
 Dans ce rôle, vous dirigerez les pratiques d’architecture qui relient la stratégie d’affaires à l’exécution technologique. Vous collaborerez avec les dirigeants, les équipes produits, ingénierie, sécurité, opérations et les parties prenantes métier afin de moderniser les plateformes, simplifier les environnements hérités, orienter la stratégie d’expérience numérique et renforcer la gouvernance architecturale. Vous développerez également les talents, influencerez les décisions à l’échelle de l’entreprise et aiderez les équipes à livrer des solutions technologiques à fort impact dans un environnement complexe et réglementé.

 Ce que vous ferez

 Diriger la pratique d’architecture d’entreprise couvrant l’architecture de solutions, l’architecture applicative, la modernisation et la gestion de l’expérience numérique.
 Définir les normes d’architecture, les feuilles de route, les modèles de gouvernance et les cadres décisionnels permettant une livraison technologique sécurisée et évolutive.
 Collaborer avec les dirigeants et les responsables métier afin d’aligner la stratégie d’architecture sur les objectifs d’affaires, les besoins des clients et les priorités de l’entreprise.
 Diriger les stratégies de modernisation des applications et plateformes héritées, y compris la rationalisation applicative, la migration vers le cloud, l’intégration, l’automatisation et la réduction de la dette technique.
 Orienter l’architecture de l’expérience numérique afin d’améliorer l’utilisabilité, l’accessibilité, la performance, la fiabilité ainsi que les parcours clients et employés de bout en bout.
 Conseiller les équipes sur les modèles d’architecture modernes, notamment les API, les microservices, les plateformes cloud natives, l’intégration de données, la gestion des identités, la sécurité et l’observabilité.
 Superviser la planification du portefeuille d’architecture, la stratégie fournisseurs, les recommandations d’investissement et la création de valeur mesurable.
 Développer les responsables et les équipes d’architecture grâce au mentorat, à la gestion des talents, à l’évaluation de la performance et à un leadership inclusif.

 Exigences de base

 13 ans ou plus d’expérience professionnelle en technologie, dont au moins 6 ans dans des fonctions de leadership en architecture, ingénierie, livraison d’applications, plateformes numériques ou transformation technologique. 
 Diplôme universitaire en informatique, systèmes d’information, ingénierie ou domaine connexe, ou expérience équivalente.
 Expérience dans la direction d’architectures d’entreprise, de solutions ou applicatives dans des environnements technologiques de grande envergure.
 Expérience de la conception et de la modernisation d’architectures de solutions d’entreprise en s’appuyant sur des plateformes intégrant l’intelligence artificielle et des technologies émergentes afin de stimuler l’innovation, l’évolutivité et la création de valeur.
 Expérience dans l’élaboration de stratégies d’architecture, de feuilles de route, de normes, de modèles de gouvernance et de recommandations destinées aux dirigeants.
 Expérience dans la modernisation d’applications, de plateformes ou de capacités numériques héritées.
 Expérience en gestion de responsables, d’équipes d’architecture ou d’équipes technologiques multidisciplinaires.
 Expérience de collaboration avec des parties prenantes métier et technologiques de haut niveau pour influencer la stratégie et l’exécution.
 Expérience en planification budgétaire, gestion des fournisseurs, priorisation de portefeuille ou prise de décisions d’investissement technologique.

 Compétences et expériences privilégiées

 Expérience avec les plateformes cloud, les stratégies API, les microservices, l’architecture événementielle (event-driven), le DevSecOps ou l’ingénierie de plateformes.
 Expérience en gestion de l’expérience numérique, plateformes d’expérience client, portails, applications mobiles/web ou solutions omnicanales.
 Expérience dans les secteurs de la santé, de la distribution pharmaceutique, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, du commerce de détail ou d’autres environnements d’entreprise réglementés.
 Expérience des cadres d’architecture d’entreprise, des comités de revue d’architecture, de la modélisation des capacités ou de la gestion de portefeuille applicatif.
 Expérience de direction de programmes de transformation à grande échelle impliquant plusieurs équipes, fonctions ou unités d’affaires.
 Excellentes compétences en communication avec les dirigeants et capacité à simplifier des décisions technologiques complexes pour des audiences métier.
 Capacité démontrée à améliorer la performance opérationnelle, réduire la dette technique et accélérer la mise sur le marché.
 Style de leadership axé sur la collaboration, la vision stratégique, la conduite du changement, l’orientation client et le développement des talents.

 Déplacements, présence au bureau et exigences physiques

 Le modèle de travail peut être à distance, hybride ou en présentiel selon les besoins de l’entreprise et de l’équipe.
 Des déplacements occasionnels peuvent être requis pour des réunions de leadership, des sessions de planification, des rencontres avec des fournisseurs ou des activités de collaboration d’équipe.
 Le poste requiert une utilisation régulière de l’ordinateur ainsi qu’une participation à des réunions virtuelles et en personne.

jobs.description:
Who We Are 

 At Momentum Financial Services Group, we help people move forward by reimagining how money works for those who need it most. With more than 40 years of experience, we’re the team behind Money Mart—Canada’s largest non-bank branch network—and a leader in financial solutions for underserved communities.

 From short-term loans to money transfers and prepaid cards, we power the products, technology, and operations that connect over a million customers a year to the money they need, when they need it.

 At MFSG, we come together across teams and departments to create something bigger than ourselves: solutions that remove barriers and give people access to money they might not get anywhere else. Whether you're solving problems, building systems, or shaping strategy, your work fuels real support for real people.

 We’ve Got You Covered 

 Compensation Philosophy: Our strategy is designed to attract and retain top talent by offering competitive, fair, and performance-driven rewards. We benchmark against the market, recognize strong performance and continuously evolve to meet the needs of our people and our business.

 Discretionary Annual Bonus: Enjoy the opportunity for a discretionary bonus based on individual performance and company success.

 Comprehensive Benefits: Our benefits include health and dental plans with 100% of the premiums covered. We also offer an Employee Assistance Program to support your mental well-being and provide resources for personal challenges.

 Retirement Plans: Plan for your future with our robust retirement savings options, ensuring you’re set for the long haul.

 Hybrid Work Environment: Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work model, allowing you to balance remote work with in-office.

 Perks and Rewards: Enjoy reimbursement for tuition assistance and professional development, discounts through Perkopolis and participate in our rewards and recognition programs to celebrate your contributions.

 What You’ll Do 

 The Job:  Director, Data Architecture & Information Management

 As the  Director, Data Architecture & Information Management, you will serve as the organization’s designated authority and strategic leader for enterprise data architecture. Working across major business and technology initiatives, you will influence key decisions and lead the evolution of the enterprise data systems architecture, enterprise data model, and Master Data Management (MDM) capabilities.

 This leadership role is accountable for setting the strategic direction for data and establishing the standards, patterns, information models, and architecture review processes that govern how data is designed, integrated, and managed across the enterprise. Through this work, you will enable trusted, scalable, and reusable information assets that support business operations, analytics, digital initiatives, and AI capabilities.

 What You’ll Do 

 Provide architectural leadership and design oversight across major projects, programs, and technology initiatives that impact enterprise data.

 Partner with business and technology leaders to define future-state data capabilities and architecture roadmaps aligned with strategic priorities.

 Define and lead the organization’s Master Data Management (MDM) strategy, architecture, and roadmap, beginning with customer data and expanding across additional domains.

 Own and evolve the enterprise canonical data model and business information architecture to improve consistency, interoperability, reuse, and scalability.

 Establish and govern enterprise data architecture standards, design patterns, information models, reference architectures, and architecture review processes.

 Lead enterprise data modeling, metadata architecture, information lifecycle management, and related architectural practices.

 Evaluate emerging technologies, data platforms, and AI capabilities to strengthen the enterprise data architecture and create business value.

 Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team of Data Architects, Data Modelers, and Data Engineers..

 What You’ll Bring 

 Required Qualifications 

 Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Systems, Engineering, Data Management, or a related discipline.

 10+ years of progressive experience in enterprise data architecture, information architecture, data modeling, and information management.

 Proven success influencing enterprise-wide business and technology decisions through architectural leadership.

 Experience partnering with Enterprise, Solution, and Cloud Architects to establish end-to-end architecture strategies.

 Demonstrated experience designing and implementing enterprise data standards, architecture patterns, and governance processes.

 Strong expertise in conceptual, logical, and physical data modeling.

 Experience leading Master Data Management (MDM) initiatives and enterprise information management programs.

 Experience developing enterprise information models, integration standards, and reference architectures.

 Proven ability to collaborate with senior business and technology leaders to define future-state architecture roadmaps.

 Preferred Qualifications 

 Master’s degree in a related discipline.

 Experience within financial services or another highly regulated industry.

 Experience designing or supporting modern cloud-based data platforms, preferably Snowflake.

 Experience with modern data transformation and modeling practices using dbt or similar technologies.

 Experience enabling AI, advanced analytics, customer intelligence, and digital transformation initiatives.

 Experience building and leading architecture or information management teams.

 Committed to Equal Opportunity: 

 MFSG is committed to accommodating applicants up to the point of undue hardship during the recruitment, assessment and selection process. If you are selected for an interview, please notify MFSG if you require accommodation in respect of the materials or procedures used at any time during this process. If you require accommodation, MFSG will work with you to determine how to meet your needs.
 About MFSG – Our Commitment to Responsible Innovation

 At MFSG, we are committed to building innovative solutions grounded in ethical, transparent, and responsible use of data and technology. Aligned with the principles outlined in Canada’s Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA), we take a proactive approach to ensuring that any AI or data-driven systems we use are safe, fair, and accountable. We may use AI to screen, assess or select applicants.  

 This posting is for a current position within our organization, offering the opportunity to contribute to meaningful, responsible innovation that supports our employees, clients, and communities. 

 We prioritize strong data governance, clear communication around how systems work, and safeguards that reduce risks and protect individuals. Our focus is on developing tools and processes that promote equity, reliability, and trust, supported by ongoing monitoring and continuous improvement.

 Joining MFSG means contributing to a future-focused organization that values both innovation and integrity, where your work helps shape solutions that responsibly support our employees, clients, and communities.

 Cyber Risk Management & Governance: 

 Own and operate the enterprise cyber risk management framework

 Maintain cybersecurity, technology, and data risk registers

 Conduct cyber risk assessments across business processes, systems, vendors, and strategic initiatives

 Define and track key risk indicators (KRIs), metrics, and remediation activities

 Support post-incident risk reviews and continuous improvement efforts

 Build strong relationships across cybersecurity, IT, legal, compliance, enterprise risk, and operational teams

 Personally execute critical deliverables in a hands-on leadership capacity

 Balance business objectives with practical, risk-based governance and security controls

 10+ years of experience in information security, cybersecurity, technology risk, or IT controls

 At least 5 years of direct GRC experience, including 3+ years in a leadership capacity

 Experience within banking, fintech, insurance, payments, wealth management, or another regulated financial services environment

 Proven success operating as a senior individual contributor with ownership of risk assessments, governance documentation, executive reporting, and remediation tracking

 Strong understanding of enterprise cyber risk management, governance, and compliance practices

 Extensive experience with data governance risk management, privacy controls, and information asset protection

 Experience managing cyber risk registers, risk reviews, issue management, and remediation programs

 Strong knowledge of Canadian financial sector regulatory expectations, operational resilience principles, and privacy obligations

 Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate technical issues into clear business risk language

 Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Computer Science, Risk Management, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

 Experience supporting audits, regulatory reviews, customer security assessments, and control testing activities

 Strong understanding of identity and access management, data protection, cloud security, vulnerability management, incident response, third-party risk, and business continuity

 Preferred Qualifications 

 Experience within a Canadian regulated financial institution or fintech organization

 Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CGEIT, or ISO 27001 Lead Implementer/Auditor

 Experience implementing or enhancing GRC platforms, workflow automation, and reporting dashboards

 Familiarity with PCI DSS, SOC 2, cloud control frameworks, and privacy control frameworks

With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work. 
 
At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. It all starts with our hiring practices where we uncover AI expertise that complements our mission, and we continue to invest in training and development to nurture innovation throughout the employee journey.
 
Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.
 
 
**Travel to Office expectations**
For Remote Roles: If this role is remote, there will be in-office events that will require travel to and from the Mississauga and/or Salt Lake City office. These will include, but not limited to, onboarding, team events, semi-annual and annual team meetings.
 
For Hybrid Roles: If this role is Hybrid, there will be an expectation to reside within commutable distance to the office/location specified in the job listing. This will include, but not limited to, weekly/bi-weekly/monthly events in the office with your specific team. This is a requirement for this role.


Team Summary:
Our team of five Partner Managers owns the full partner lifecycle, from identifying and prioritizing partners through negotiation, go-to-market planning and execution, and ongoing performance management. As Director, you’ll lead this team while also playing a central role in our data strategy, helping evolve and execute authorized data access pathways for both customers and third-party vendors. This is a high-impact opportunity to shape how our partner ecosystem and data strategy work together as an organizational priority. The role can be performed remotely or from one of our offices, so you can work where you do your best work.
 
Job Summary:
Director, Partnerships & Data Strategy is responsible for developing and maintaining the Partner Powered Solutions strategy, managing the entire life cycle of partner relationships (identification, prioritization, negotiation, GTM planning & execution, and ongoing performance management). The role requires an individual who is a strategic thinker with a demonstrated ability to act individually where required but also lead and improve team efficiency and effectiveness through the creation and continued optimization of process and approach. In addition, the Director leads PointClickCare's Data Strategy, supporting the organizational imperative to evolve and execute authorized data access pathways for both customers and third-party vendors. This requires working closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Corporate Development, Legal and Regulatory to define and execute a Data Strategy roadmap aligned to market needs, voice of customer, and regulatory requirements, while cultivating the third-party vendor relationships and internal enablement needed to bring that roadmap to market.

Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.
 
About the Team
The People Strategy & Transformation (PST) is PointClickCare's HR strategy, organizational design, and portfolio management pillar. The team includes HR Business Partners, Organizational Design & Effectiveness, People Experience, and the HR Strategy & Enablement function, with a dotted-line partnership to Internal Communications. PST is responsible for ensuring HR's work across every Center of Excellence is planned, resourced, sequenced, and tracked against business outcomes — spanning a portfolio of Pillar Initiatives, Cross-Pillar Projects, and Program Roll-Ups delivered across all four HR solution groups.
 
Position Summary:
The Director, People Strategy and HR Portfolio (Project) Management s is the VP, People Strategy & Transformation's strategic thought partner in building and running PointClickCare's HR Portfolio Management Office (HR PMO) — co-designing the strategy, governance model, capacity methodology, and dashboard reporting that let HR plan, resource, and track its work against business outcomes. This is a net-new function: no HR PMO currently exists at PointClickCare, and this role will design these mechanics in partnership with the VP rather than operate a system someone else has already built.

Operating with significant design authority but without direct reports or final decision rights on cross-functional trade-offs, this role earns influence through the credibility of the mechanics it builds and runs. It operates across all four HR solution groups without formal authority over any of them, serves as the VP's thought partner on HR strategy and the HR SLT prioritization process, and convenes HR initiative stakeholders and Internal Communications to coordinate how HR's work reaches the business.
 
Key Responsibilities:
Design and run the HR Portfolio Management Office’s core operating mechanics
Design and maintain the capacity management methodology, including the heat map model and the oversubscription thresholds used to flag resourcing conflicts across HR COEs
Own and run the Portfolio Council governance cadence end to end — intake, capacity check, tier assignment, publish, mid-quarter check, and close-out
Build and maintain the integrated HR initiative dashboard, ensuring data currency and accuracy across every active Pillar Initiative, Cross-Pillar Project, and Program Roll-Up
Example deliverable: a quarterly Portfolio Council capacity heat map showing every HR COE’s current initiative load, used to approve or defer new initiative intake
Serve as strategic thought partner to the VP, People Strategy & Transformation
Co-design the HR SLT prioritization process and criteria used to evaluate and sequence HR initiatives each planning cycle
Co-design the OKR and scorecard measurement architecture — what gets measured, how it rolls up, and the cadence it runs on
Co-author and stress-test the HR Strategy on a Page, contributing independent analysis before it is finalized by the VP
Example deliverable: a documented HR SLT prioritization framework — criteria, weighting, and process — adopted for the FY28 planning cycle
Own capacity management and project plan oversight across the full HR initiative portfolio
Track progress against committed business outcomes, not activity completion alone, across every active HR initiative
Maintain consistent project plan structure, milestone tracking, and dependency mapping in partnership with each initiative’s named Delivery Lead
Proactively surface cross-COE capacity collisions and resourcing conflicts before they reach Portfolio Council
Example deliverable: a consolidated project plan view across all active Program Roll-Ups, flagging dependency risk before it affects a committed milestone
Convene HR initiative stakeholders and Internal Communications on a recurring cadence
Establish and run a recurring go-to-market coordination cadence bringing together initiative Delivery Leads and Internal Communications
Sequence the timing and stakeholder readiness of HR initiative rollouts to the business, avoiding duplicate or conflicting messages landing in the same window
Maintain a shared go-to-market calendar visible to HR SLT, showing what is launching, when, and to whom
Example deliverable: a quarterly HR go-to-market calendar sequencing every planned initiative rollout to the business, reviewed and approved by HR SLT before the quarter begins
Represent HR in enterprise planning and governance forums
Serve as the primary operational liaison to the Strategic Delivery Office, aligning HR’s initiative classification and intake practices to enterprise taxonomy
Represent HR’s initiative portfolio and capacity picture in the Corporate Strategy Group’s quarterly planning cadence
Flag enterprise-level dependencies or conflicts affecting HR’s ability to deliver against committed priorities
Example deliverable: HR’s consolidated initiative and capacity submission into the Corporate Strategy Group’s quarterly planning sprint, reflecting current Portfolio Council status
 
Required Skills & Qualifications:
10–15 years of experience in program/portfolio management, management consulting, or a PMO leadership capacity, including demonstrated experience designing — not only operating — portfolio governance, capacity management, or OKR measurement systems
A track record serving as a strategic thought partner to a senior leader, with evidence of shaping that leader's thinking rather than only executing direction
Demonstrated experience operating in matrixed, cross-functional environments without formal authority over the teams being coordinated
Strong data and dashboard fluency — comfortable architecting reporting tools and the metrics model behind them, not just maintaining an existing build
Executive-level communication skills — this role prepares materials for and interacts directly with VP-level stakeholders across every HR pillar
Experience convening cross-functional stakeholder groups to coordinate sequencing and alignment on complex, multi-team initiatives
 
Preferred Experience:
Experience building a PMO or governance function from scratch, in a design capacity, rather than operating within an already-mature one
HR domain experience, including familiarity with COE structures and business-outcome-linked workforce initiatives
Experience partnering with internal communications or marketing functions on coordinated, multi-stakeholder rollouts

 At RBC Insurance, AI is fundamental to transforming how we operate, serve our customers, and compete in a rapidly evolving financial services landscape. You'll be responsible for building the intelligent, data-driven foundation that enables RBC Insurance to unlock AI-driven intelligence to enhance customer experiences, and fundamentally transform our business model. This is your opportunity to lead one of the most consequential technology transformations in our organization's history.

 What will you do?   

 Own enterprise AI strategy and delivery: Develop and execute the long-term vision for AI capabilities across RBC Insurance IT and business operations. Identify frontier, game-changing AI use cases that drive competitive advantage, serve as the expert for emerging AI technologies, and position RBC Insurance as an AI-first organization.
 Architect and modernize data platforms: Lead the strategic transformation of our global data foundation, stabilizing and enhancing both on-premises and cloud data platforms.  What's the opportunity? 

 We're looking for a product leader to own the roadmap for RBC's internal agentic AI platform end-to-end — from intake and prioritization through delivery and measurement. As Director, Product Strategy & Roadmap, you will decide what ships and when, ground those decisions in user value and adoption evidence, and own the product experience and analytics that make the platform usable and valuable at scale.

 You will bring rigour to prioritization, fluency in agentic AI, and the credibility to partner with engineering on how the roadmap gets built — without owning the technical implementation.

 Your responsibilities will include: 
 Roadmap ownership: Maintaining and communicating a rolling 12-month roadmap with clear, evidence-based prioritization rationale

 User experience: Owning the end-to-end product experience across the platform — how users discover, adopt, build with, and get value from it — including the self-service builder, templates, and connector catalog as part of a coherent whole.

 Product analytics: Building and maintaining adoption dashboards, usage telemetry, and value-realization measurement to drive decisions

 Have 8+ years of product management experience, including 3+ in AI/ML products or enterprise platforms

 Have a deep working understanding of agentic AI: LLMs, tool-use, MCP connectors, RAG, and multi-agent orchestration

 Senior Director, AI Product Management

 We're looking for a product leader who can turn a strategic product vision into shipped reality at scale. You will build discipline around ensuring relentless customer focus and a business-strategy lens on what we build and why. You will lead a team of Product Managers and own Voice of the Customer, feature prioritization, adoption and community building around the product across RBC.
 You will be expected to set the operating rhythm, make the hard tradeoff and resourcing calls, and hold a quality bar — bringing the credibility that comes from having built and shipped AI products at scale, not just managed roadmaps.

 Your responsibilities will include: 
 Team leadership: Leading and developing Director-level leads (across Product Strategy & Roadmap, Community & Adoption, Ecosystem & Partnerships) and the teams beneath them, with clear career paths and succession

 Integrated delivery: Owning a single execution plan that aligns roadmap delivery, community programs, and partnership milestones to one cadence

 Operating cadence: Establishing and running sprint reviews, quarterly planning, and OKR setting and tracking

 Tradeoff and escalation ownership: Serving as the primary escalation point for cross-pillar dependencies, tradeoffs, and resourcing decisions

 Product quality: Maintaining acceptance criteria, release gates, and documentation standards across the squad

 Adoption and outcomes: Using analytics, telemetry, and adoption measurement to drive decisions and report progress, risks, and resource needs

 Ecosystem health: Ensuring the community and partnership programs sustain engagement and healthy adoption across the RBC user base

 You're our ideal candidate if you: 
 Have 10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years leading multi-team product organizations as a manager of managers

 Have a track record of customer discovery and translating user needs into product strategy and prioritization

 Have hands-on experience delivering end-user facing AI products — ideally generative or agentic AI — at production scale

 Have run large-scale internal or enterprise product launches with measurable adoption outcomes

 Bring strong operational discipline: agile delivery, OKR frameworks, and release management

jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What’s the Opportunity? 
 Newcomers are critical client segment for RBC, with distinct needs across their journey - from preparing to move to Canada, to establishing their financial lives upon arrival, to building deeper financial relationships as they settle and grow.
 As Director, Newcomer Channel Strategy & Operations, you will lead the strategy and evolution of the channels, capabilities and partnership operations required to deliver a differentiated newcomer banking proposition. You will own the "how" behind our newcomer strategy: translating our ambition into intuitive client journeys, scalable capabilities, effective frontline experiences and an ecosystem of services that helps newcomers establish their lives in Canada.
 This is a highly cross-functional role. You will work across Everyday Banking & Client Growth, Product, Digital, Enablement, Advice Centre, Technology, Risk, Compliance, Marketing, and external partners to identify friction, establish priorities, and mobilize the organization around a multi-year newcomer journey.

 What You'll Do 
 Own the End-To-End Newcomer Onboarding Experience 
 Develop and continuously evolve the target experience for newcomers across key moments in their journey - from pre-arrival through onboarding, settlement, and early relationship growth

 Identify the highest impact experience gaps, friction points, and capability opportunities
 Define the target state newcomer experience and work cross-functionally to define it into a prioritized roadmap
 Establish clear experience principles and standards that can be applied across products and channels
