 Own the Pre-Arrival Account Open Capability 
 Own and continuously evolve the end-to-end pre-arrival account open capability, ensuring a seamless accessible and differentiated experience for newcomers establishing their relationship before coming to Canada
 Define the strategic direction and prioritized roadmap for pre-arrival account opening, identifying opportunities to enhance functionality, simplify the client experience and expand acquisition opportunities
 Identify and address capability gaps, client friction points, and operational inefficiencies across the pre-arrival account opening journey, from application and identity verification through account activation and funding
 Partner with Digital, Product, Technology, Business Development, Operations and Risk teams to deliver capability enhancements that balance client experience, business growth, operational scalability and regulatory requirements
 Identify opportunities to expand the reach and effectiveness of pre-arrival account opening across priority newcomer markets, acquisition channels and strategic partnerships

 Lead the efforts to remove unnecessary complexity from how newcomers establish a banking relationship while ensuring appropriate risk and regulatory requirements are maintained
 Identify policies or processes creating disproportionate friction for newcomers

 Challenge legacy processes and distinguish true regulatory requirements from internal practices
 Design scalable solutions that balance client experience, growth, operational simplicity and risk

 Partner with digital and journey teams to influence enterprise capability roadmaps
 Work with distribution leaders to understand frontline friction and execution gaps
 Ensure new capabilities and propositions can be delivered consistently across channels

 Must-have 
 8+ years of experience in strategy, client experience, digital transformation, product management, operations or financial services.

jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 
 Join our U.S. Technology Strategy and Architecture team as Director, Technology Product Strategy, where you will play a key role in supporting the development and execution of technology strategy across RBC’s U.S. organization.
 Working closely with U.S. Technology Strategy & Architecture leadership, business lines, technology teams, and enterprise architecture, you will help shape the strategic direction of the U.S. technology organization. You will analyze the technology landscape, support strategic planning and investment decisions, and work across business and technology teams to advance key priorities.
 This role provides broad exposure across the U.S. technology organization and an opportunity to work on some of its most important strategic questions. You will combine structured problem solving, technology knowledge, stakeholder management, and executive communication to support senior leaders in making informed technology decisions and advancing the U.S. technology agenda.

 What will you do? 
 Support target-state strategy development:  Partner with Technology Strategy & Architecture leadership to develop and maintain forward-looking U.S. technology strategy and, where required, business-line technology strategies. Gather inputs, assess strategic alternatives, and translate direction into clear target-state objectives, principles, KPIs, and priorities.
 Maintain a view of the technology estate:  Develop and maintain a comprehensive view of the U.S. technology landscape, bringing together information on applications, platforms, infrastructure, capabilities, dependencies, and investments to support strategic planning and decision-making.
 Conduct strategic analyses:  Perform structured, point-in-time analyses of technology opportunities, challenges, and strategic questions. Synthesize quantitative and qualitative information, evaluate alternatives, and develop recommendations for leadership consideration.
 Support strategic alignment:  Work with business and technology stakeholders to assess the alignment of major initiatives, programs, and investments with U.S. technology strategy and enterprise priorities. Identify potential gaps or areas of misalignment and support development of appropriate actions.
 Support roadmap and funding decisions:  Develop analyses and decision materials that help leadership evaluate technology roadmaps, investment priorities, dependencies, trade-offs, and funding requirements.
 Support architecture governance and control:  Partner with Enterprise Architecture and technology teams to facilitate architecture governance activities, track strategic and architectural decisions, identify areas requiring escalation, and support alignment with established architecture principles and target states.
 Coordinate strategic planning activities:  Support recurring strategy, roadmap, portfolio, and governance processes across the U.S. technology organization, ensuring stakeholders have the information and analysis required to make timely decisions.
 Develop executive-level materials:  Translate complex technology topics into concise presentations, recommendations, business cases, and decision materials for senior technology and business leadership.
 Monitor strategic progress:  Develop and maintain KPIs, KRIs, and other measures that provide visibility into progress against technology strategies, roadmaps, strategic initiatives, and architectural objectives.
 Build organizational capability:  Support the development and adoption of frameworks, methodologies, tools, templates, and ways of working that strengthen technology strategy and architecture capabilities across the U.S. organization.
 Facilitate cross-functional collaboration:  Coordinate across business lines, technology teams, architecture, finance, risk, and other stakeholders to gather inputs, resolve issues, and support decisions on cross-cutting technology priorities.
 Identify emerging issues and opportunities:  Analyze trends across the technology estate and external technology landscape to identify potential capability gaps, duplication, architectural constraints, emerging technologies, and opportunities for strategic improvement.

 What do you need to succeed? 
 Must have: 
 Undergraduate degree or equivalent experience in technology, business, engineering, finance, or a related field.

 Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into clear presentations and decision materials.
 Strong stakeholder management skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively across business and technology organizations.
 Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work in a complex, matrixed environment.
 Strong understanding of technology and/or the financial services industry.
 Experience using current AI tooling to support research, automate repetitive tasks, analyze large data sets, etc.

 Experience in financial services or another highly regulated industry.
 Experience in a matrix environment, such as a large, publicly traded corporation.

jobs.title: Head of Toronto AI Center
jobs.description:
Lab Summary: 

 Samsung Research America (SRA) develops next-generation technologies in software, user experience, and services for future products. Headquartered in Silicon Valley with locations across North America, we partner with industry and academia to translate research and innovation into tangible outcomes. We lead in machine intelligence by building AI that is user-centric and physically grounded—AI that understands not just what users want, but their physical context and environment.

 Samsung is uniquely positioned to bring this vision to life through nearly 500 million connected devices we sell annually. Our mission is to holistically integrate AI into connected ecosystems—homes, offices, robotics, and beyond—creating a platform that scales quickly while providing deep contextual understanding and spatial awareness.

   The AI Center in Toronto, Canada plays a pivotal role in developing next-generation software, user experiences, and intelligent services that enrich consumers’ lives. This lab actively contributes to the international research community through publications and presentations at major conferences.

   Areas of Research: 

 Computer Vision

 Contextual/Multi-Modal Modeling

 3D Perception & Scene Understanding

 Inference and Reasoning

 Machine and Deep Learning

 Human Computer Interaction (HCI)

 Natural Language Processing

 Position Summary: 

 Samsung’s AI research team in Toronto is looking for an outstanding and highly self-motivated leader to head the lab. The candidates should have extensive expertise in deep learning, computer vision and physics-based AI.

 The AI research center is a key part of Samsung’s global R&D effort and aims to have direct impact on future Samsung products reaching hundreds of millions of users globally. The candidate will work with a team of research scientists and engineers tackling real-world problems involving Samsung’s Artificial intelligence products. The candidate can also have the opportunity to publish at top-tier conferences in deep learning, computer vision, and language understanding.

 Position Responsibilities: 

 Build, manage, develop, lead, and support the AI research team, with the outcome of high-impact research insights that influence the product roadmap

 Present research findings and insights both within and outside of the company

 Serve as a thought partner with the executive, cross-functional, and line of business leadership teams

 Be an evangelist of research practices throughout the company, influencing partner teams

 Drive innovation programs within the relevant fields of Artificial Intelligence,

 Serve as the external face for the AI Research Lab’s advanced technology capabilities

 Drive key University technology collaboration program to build long term innovation partnerships

 Lead Technology Pathfinding to understand key technology trends and impact for Samsung, to help drive growth and new business opportunities for Samsung

   Required Skills: 

 PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience

 10+ years of post-PhD experience leading advanced AI research.

 Deep expertise in vision and multimodal AI and agentic AI (autonomous agents, reasoning, decision-making), plus strong foundations in computer vision, image/video processing, and generative AI applications.

 Significant experience of publishing relevant peer-reviewed articles on artificial intelligence

 Strong algorithmic problem-solving skills, and the ability to program in C/C++, Python, Java, etc.

 Experience in publishing scientific papers in top quality conferences/journals (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, IJCAI, ACL, SIGGRAPH, CoRL, etc.)

 Experience in DL library such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, etc. with strong hands on experience is required

 Experience working with GPU, parallel programming, and Simulation environments is a plus

 Experience in Android development and graphic rendering is a plus

 Ability to work well in a fast-paced global team environment

 Strong network of relationships with entrepreneurs, VC’s industry executives, and technology thought leaders

 Strong presentation skills and excellent interpersonal skills

jobs.description:

 What you'll do 
 Prospecting & lead generation: Identify and target potential customers through research, networking, and cold calling. Build new relationships with our enterprise customers and prospects to drive revenue, pipeline, and deployment capacity.

 Manage relationships: Build and maintain strong relationships with key decision-makers and stakeholders with our largest customers. Serve as their primary point of contact and exceed their expectations.

 Negotiating & closing complex deal cycles: Lead negotiations with existing and prospective customers, addressing objections and closing deals. Navigate contracts and agreements quickly and effectively, working closely with legal and finance stakeholders.

 Sales strategy & planning: Develop and execute sales strategies to meet or exceed sales targets. Craft tailored sales presentations and proposals that meet our enterprise customers needs. Collaborate with our marketing team to implement effective sales campaigns and presentations.

 Collaborate cross-functionally: Work closely with our broader GTM team, as well as our product, technical and operations orgs to deliver our industry-leading product.

 Operate as an AI-native seller: Leverage AI tools across the full sales cycle- account research, personalized outreach, call summarization, pipeline forecasting, and deal execution- to automate low-value tasks and reinvest that time into high-value customer relationships, while continuously adopting and experimenting with new tools to work faster and smarter than traditional methods allow.

 What you'll bring 
 6-8 years of experience in an enterprise customer-facing sales role, identifying and closing large accounts.

 Enterprise experience: Experience managing a $1M+ quota and running end-to-end complex 6- and 7-figure ACV deals.

 Strong communication skills: Exceptional verbal and written communication abilities.

 Analytical mindset: Ability to analyze market trends, identify opportunities, and make data-driven decisions.

 Prospecting & lead generation: Proven track record of identifying and targeting potential enterprise clients through research, networking, and cold calling.

 Even better... 
 Industry knowledge: Familiarity with the AI landscape, key players, and emerging trends.

 Our values 
 Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

 Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

 Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

 Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

 Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.

 We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:
 Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

 Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

 Life insurance and disability benefits

 Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

 Parental leave

 Fertility and family building benefits

 Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized when working onsite

 Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

 Free alphorn lessons

jobs.title: Director, Corporate Risk Information Management
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do. 

 At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

 When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

 Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

 Job Description: 
 About the role 

 Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, Emerging Risk Management & Strategic Risk Initiatives, the Director, Corporate Risk Information Management is accountable for the oversight of the information management, records management, and data governance policy requirements and underlying programs across Corporate Risk, which includes Enterprise & Operational Risk Management, Insurance & Financial Risk Management, Investment & Credit Risk Management, and the Corporate and DBTS Business Group Risk Office teams. The Director sets direction, maintains the framework and methodology, and holds Information Stewards, Records Officers, Records Custodians, Data Custodians and Risk Office teams accountable so that information assets are properly classified, protected, retained, disposed of, and governed in alignment with the Enterprise Information Management Policy, regulatory expectations, and business needs. The Director leads continuous improvement of the program, including enhancements to tools, and strengthens program governance, effectiveness, and efficiency.

 The Director is the accountable owner for structured and non-structured business records and information assets within Corporate Risk, in line with the Enterprise Information Management Policy.

 The role holds the Records Steward, Records Officer, Data Governance Operational Lead, and Non-Structured Data Information Stewardship accountabilities for Corporate Risk, reflecting the centralized operating model of the function. It provides integrated oversight of information lifecycle management, repository governance, data quality, metadata, reporting, and information risk management, and ensures consistent execution of records and information management requirements across Corporate Risk.

 What you'll be doing 

 Lead information governance, risk, and compliance
 Serve as the accountable lead for Non-Structured Information Management governance for Corporate Risk.
 Maintain the Corporate Risk information management framework, operating guidelines, and standards, aligned to the Enterprise Information Management Policy, and oversee adherence to policy and related control expectations.
 Provide guidance and advice to Business Group Risk Office teams and business leaders when judgement or clarification is required on information governance obligations, risks, and implementation requirements. Provide advice into strategic decisions and program improvements.
 On a quarterly basis, independently evaluate the Corporate Risk information management risk profile, including Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), and report results, material non-compliance, and significant issues to senior management and the Operational Risk and Compliance Committee (ORCC) in a timely manner.
 Oversee and coordinate Corporate Risk's response to Risk Control Self Assessments, audits, compliance reviews, and regulatory examinations, and oversee related issue remediation activities related to information management.
 Prepare an annual report to senior management and ORCC on the status of the information management, records management, and data governance program.
 Establish, maintain, and continually enhance the oversight and monitoring frameworks for the program.
 Monitor and benchmark Corporate Risk information management practices against industry standards, regulatory expectations, and best practices, and assess complex information risk issues to guide solution recommendations.
 Develop and own the short- and mid-term strategy and roadmap for information management, records management, and data governance in Corporate Risk, aligned to enterprise and Business Group strategy, and provide significant input to Corporate Risk's strategic and long-term plans.
 Set program roll out objectives and plan and prioritize program resources, milestones, and dependencies across Corporate Risk.

 Records and information lifecycle management
 Direct and oversee records management activities, including records classification, retention, legal holds, disposition, and remediation planning.
 Perform and oversee Records Officer responsibilities for Corporate Risk, retaining accountability for consistent execution of records management requirements, guidance, monitoring, and issue follow-up.
 Oversee Records Impact Assessments (RIAs) and Records Management Risk Reviews when new or changed processes, systems, repositories, vendors, or operating models may affect the creation, storage, access, retention, transfer, or disposition of Corporate Risk business records, and provide guidance on complex or high-risk cases.
 Oversee the maintenance of records and repository inventories and ensure ownership and stewardship assignments remain current.
 Determine how Corporate Risk business records are identified, classified, captured, stored, protected, retained, and disposed of, and hold Records Custodians accountable for applying those determinations.
 Make final decisions within Corporate Risk on record designation, retention and disposition, legal hold implementation, and exceptions to records requirements, and escalate only matters that require enterprise policy interpretation or an exception to enterprise policy.

 Advance data governance and repository oversight
 Provide oversight and approval of Data Governance artifacts and Business Impact Statements prepared by Information Stewards.
 Lead data quality, metadata, business glossary, lineage, classification, and critical information inventory practices, including the related standards and methodology.
 Monitor and report Data Governance KPIs and oversee remediation of identified issues.
 Lead governance of SharePoint, Teams, shared mailboxes, network drives, and other non-structured business repositories.

 Enable change and stakeholder engagement
 Build strong working relationships with Information Owners, Records Custodians, Information Custodians, Risk Offices, Compliance, Legal, Technology, Data Governance teams, and other relevant teams involved in records and data management to drive execution of key deliverables within the Three Lines of Defense model.
 Develop, maintain, and deliver training, communications, and practical guidance to Information Stewards, Records Custodians, Risk Office teams, and other stakeholders to support adoption of information governance practices.
 Lead cross-functional discussions to resolve issues, mature governance practices, and embed sustainable ways of working.
 Represent Corporate Risk on peer Steering Groups and provide direction on information management matters.
 Work closely with Business Group Risk Office teams on the effective roll-out of program changes.
 Develop and communicate the vision for information governance in Corporate Risk and build consensus on operating goals aligned with the Risk division.

 What you'll need to succeed 

 University degree in Information Management, Data Governance, Records Management, Business Administration, Risk Management, Library Sciences, Information Technology, or a related discipline, and/or relevant certification.
 5+ years of risk management, records management, data governance, or information governance experience, with a proven track record of designing and implementing effective programs, controls, and processes, ideally within a major federally regulated financial institution.
 Direct experience writing policies and guidelines, and implementing governance frameworks, standards, controls, or enterprise operating procedures.
 Demonstrable experience leading cross-functional initiatives, developing strong working relationships, and influencing senior stakeholders in a large, matrixed organization within the Three Lines of Defense model.
 Proven experience dealing with complexity and ambiguity, using broad knowledge, keen analysis, and sound professional judgement to arrive at quality decisions.
 Working knowledge of Sunlife’s information management, records management, data governance, privacy, compliance, and operational risk practices.
 Ability to translate complex policy, risk, records, and data governance requirements into clear business guidance, communications, training, and sustainable operating practices.Strong knowledge of information management, records management, and data governance principles, including information lifecycle management, repository governance, metadata management, information classification, and data quality management, with the ability to assess, measure, and monitor information risk.
 Strong knowledge of the information and records management landscape, financial industry leading practices, and regulator expectations.
 Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities, with keen attention to detail, and experience in risk assessment, control design, compliance monitoring, reporting, and analytics.
 Working knowledge of Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, shared mailboxes, network drives, and other collaboration platforms.
 Experience implementing, managing, and maintaining a records, information governance, or GRC tool.
 Strategic mindset, with the ability to understand business requirements and develop innovative solutions.
 Excellent communication, facilitation, influencing, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to communicate complex concepts to a diverse audience.
 Well-developed writing and visual presentation skills to articulate analytic results, options, recommendations, and reporting.
 Effective change management and change leadership through impact and influence skills, with governance oversight and a continuous improvement mindset.• Proactive and adaptable mindset, with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced and rapidly evolving organization.

 What's in it for you: 

 Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives.
 In 2024, Sun Life ranked among the top 100 most sustainable global corporations by Corporate Knights for the 15th consecutive year, leading Canadian insurers.
 We are proud to be on the 2024 Best Workplaces in Canada list by Great Place to Work.
 We’re also listed as one of the Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams.
 Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.
 Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to support your well-being.

 The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results. 

 Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

 Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

 We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

 We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling. 

 We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

130,000/130 000 - 180,000/180 000

Risk Management

It brings an enterprise perspective to decisions, identifies opportunities for value creation and maintains strong financial management, controls and performance discipline.

 As a member of TD's leadership team, the AVP sets high ethical and performance standards, develops talent and collaborates across the Bank to deliver sustainable results. The role requires strategic insight, business acumen, sound judgment and integrity.

 POSITION-SPECIFIC ACCOUNTABILITIES:
 Lead portfolio planning, forecasting, reporting and performance management. Develop driver-based forecasts and scenarios, explain variances, and translate risks and opportunities into executive insight and recommended actions.
 Advise and independently challenge RESL pricing and offers. Assess volume, retention, margin and risk-adjusted return trade-offs, considering funding costs, customer behaviour and competition.
 Lead SSF financial planning and analysis, including MMS and broker channel financials and compensation models. Evaluate acquisition costs, incentives, conversion, retention and lifetime profitability; advise on compensation changes and channel mix across branch, specialist, broker and digital distribution.
 Assess portfolio economics across volumes, market share, margins, credit, funding, expenses and returns. Analyze profitability by product, segment and origination cohort, isolating mix, pricing, renewals and runoff. Partner with Treasury, Risk, Product and Distribution on rate scenarios, funding and capital implications.
 Advise on investment prioritization and allocation of capital, expense and capacity. Challenge business cases, returns, costs and milestones; track benefits and cross-CPSB dependencies and trade-offs. Recommend reprioritization when economics or delivery assumptions change.
 Analyze operational cost drivers, unit costs, cost-to-serve and capacity. Link volumes, service levels, staffing and demand to expense plans; challenge assumptions and identify productivity and operating-leverage opportunities while protecting controls and customer outcomes.
 Partner with COO leaders to connect strategic priorities, transformation and operating performance to financial outcomes. Assess cross-business initiatives and execution risks, balancing near-term commitments with longer-term value.
 Provide oversight and independent challenge of reporting, controls, allocations and accounting. Reinforce direct and shared cost ownership, reliable management information and consistent financial treatment; resolve issues with Finance and enterprise partners.
 Finance Talent, Capability & Leadership 
 Build a high-performing Finance team with the capabilities to deliver stronger business partnership, insight and independent challenge. Shape talent priorities, attract and develop talent, and strengthen succession and leadership depth, with a focus on commercial acumen, strategic judgment and executive influence.
 Advance the portfolio's Finance operating model in alignment with enterprise and CPSB strategy. Shape and implement changes within the team, and strengthen team capacity for higher-value advisory work.
 Champion data, digital and AI-enabled Finance, influencing priorities with enterprise partners and accelerating adoption of tools, analytics and automation that improve decision-making, information quality, productivity and colleague capacity. Provide leadership and accountability for a sound financial control environment within the portfolio. Ensure changes to processes, tools and responsibilities maintain clear ownership and effective governance; partner with enterprise control owners to address risks and sustain confidence in financial information.
 Lead through the TD Way, creating an inclusive, high-performing culture grounded in clear expectations, accountability, constructive challenge, continuous improvement and colleague development. Set clear objectives, provide ongoing coaching and feedback, recognize strong performance and address performance gaps Operate as an enterprise Finance leader, building partnerships across CPSB and enterprise Finance, Treasury, Risk, Accounting, Tax, Data & Analytics and Technology; contribute to the broader CPSB Finance agenda beyond the immediate portfolio.

 QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE: 
 The successful candidate will bring:
 Significant senior-level financial management, business advisory and leadership experience, with strong banking economics and commercial acumen.
 Strong understanding of secured lending profitability, pricing and channel economics, together with operational cost management and investment evaluation; ability to connect product, distribution and operating decisions to financial performance.
 Experience evaluating growth, investment, transformation, productivity and resource-allocation decisions, with sound judgment in balancing financial outcomes, customer needs and risk.
 Strong analytical and communication skills; ability to synthesize complex issues into concise executive recommendations and influence decisions through constructive challenge.
 Proven experience developing talent and succession depth and implementing Finance improvements across team operating models, processes, tools and controls; ability to partner with enterprise teams and deliver sustained adoption and measurable benefits.
 Ability to manage competing priorities effectively and maintain resilience in a fast-paced environment.

 EDUCATIO N
 An advanced business or professional accounting designation qualification such as MBA, CPA, or CFA, would be an asset.

 Who We Are: 
 TD is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. More than 95,000 TD colleagues bring their skills, talent, and creativity to foster deeper relationships, ensure disciplined execution, and build a simpler, faster banking experience. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing. Our Total Rewards package reflects the investments we make in our colleagues to help them and their families achieve their financial, physical, and mental well-being goals. jobs.title: VP Technology & Innovation
jobs.description:
Teladoc Health is the global virtual care leader, offering comprehensive virtual care solutions spanning virtual care including primary, mental health, expert medical, devices and licensed platform services. Teladoc Health serves the world's leading insurers, employers, and health systems and helps millions of people around the world resolve their healthcare needs with confidence. Serving over 9 million Canadians, Teladoc Health has been in Canada for more than 20 years and operates in 175 countries world-wide.

 Position Summary 

 The Vice President, Technology and Innovation (“VP”) is responsible for defining and executing Teladoc Health Canada’s technology, product, innovation and cybersecurity strategy. The VP leads the development and delivery of Teladoc Health Canada's digital products and technology ecosystem, including product management, software engineering, enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, data and analytics, technology operations, and innovation. The role is accountable for building a secure, reliable, scalable, and modern technology environment that enables high-quality virtual and hybrid care, an exceptional client, clinician, and patient experience, and operational excellence.

 The VP provides executive leadership for Teladoc Health Canada's digital strategy and multi-year technology roadmap, ensuring technology investments and product capabilities align with Canadian market needs, regulatory requirements, enterprise priorities, and Teladoc Health's global strategy. Working closely with clinical, commercial, operations, legal, privacy, compliance, and global technology leaders, the VP plays a key role in advancing Teladoc Health Canada's enterprise data governance framework and responsible use of data and AI, while delivering technology solutions that drive revenue growth, innovation, quality of care, security, and operational efficiency.

 Essential Duties and Responsibilities 

 Technology Strategy & Delivery 
 Develop and refresh Teladoc Health Canada’s digital strategy and multi-year technology roadmap aligned with organizational strategy and business objectives;

 Provide secure, scalable, resilient and sustainable digital solutions and technology infrastructure that meet Canadian business, market and regulatory requirements;

 Lead the strategy, design, development, delivery, and lifecycle management of Teladoc Health Canada’s technology ecosystem, including enterprise architecture, applications, integrations, infrastructure, and digital platforms;

 Develop and execute Teladoc Health Canada’s cybersecurity strategy, ensuring appropriate security controls, resilience, and cybersecurity risk management across technology platforms and information assets

 Own the budget, portfolio, and project management of digital initiatives and ongoing technology operations, ensuring disciplined prioritization, resource allocation, and value delivery; and

 Develop and manage strategic relationships with technology partners and vendors.

 Product Strategy & Delivery 
 Lead Teladoc Canada’s multi-year product roadmap to enable operational excellence, high-quality clinical care, commercial growth, and exceptional client, clinician and patient experiences;

 Translate market, regulatory, clinical, and operational requirements into innovative digital products;

 Champion user-centred design by incorporating the perspectives of clients, clinicians, patients, and internal users throughout the product lifecycle to deliver intuitive, accessible, and seamless digital experiences; and

 Integrate customer feedback, clinical insights, analytics, and user research into product planning, development and continuous improvement.

 Data, Analytics & AI Enablement 
 Lead the operational implementation of Teladoc Health Canada's enterprise data governance framework, including data architecture, stewardship, quality, metadata, lifecycle management, and data governance technologies, in partnership with the legal, privacy and compliance teams, and business stakeholders.

 Champion enterprise analytics, business intelligence, and AI-enabled capabilities that support operational excellence, clinical quality, innovation, and informed business decision-making.

 Develop and maintain secure, scalable, and reliable data management capabilities that enable high-quality clinical insights, operational intelligence, performance measurement, forecasting, and the responsible use of AI.

 Oversee enterprise data and analytics for the Canadian business, delivering timely, accurate, and actionable insights that support strategic planning, operational performance, and continuous improvement.

 Governance, Risk & Compliance 
 Partner with legal, privacy and compliance teams to ensure technology solutions meet applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, security, and clinical quality requirements, relevant market standards and clinical-quality expectations (e.g., PHIPA, PIPEDA, provincial health and privacy regulations, virtual care standards, responsible AI practices);

 Establish and oversee technology governance, including enterprise architecture, software development lifecycle (SDLC), cybersecurity, and cloud governance frameworks and processes, while partnering with the legal, privacy and compliance teams on enterprise data and AI governance and technology vendor risk management; and

 Identify, assess, and manage technology and cybersecurity risks by implementing appropriate controls, monitoring, and mitigation strategies to support the organization’s enterprise risk management framework, business resilience, audit readiness, and compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, and organizational requirements.

 Technology Operations & Cybersecurity 
 Ensure reliable, scalable, and secure IT operations that support business continuity, organizational growth, and compliance with applicable organizational, contractual, and regulatory requirements;

 Oversee the performance, availability, and reliability of Teladoc Health Canada’s technology ecosystem through proactive monitoring, incident management, issue triage, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement to prevent recurrence and improve system resilience;

 Provide executive oversight of Teladoc Health Canada's cybersecurity program, including information security operations, vulnerability management, identity and access management, incident response, disaster recovery, business continuity, and continuous enhancement of security controls.

 Lead technology support services for clinicians, clients, and internal users, while coordinating with Global/International teams on shared platforms, infrastructure, devices (e.g., HHS, GSD), escalation management, and operational support.

 People, Culture & Capability Building 
 Build, lead, and develop a high-performing, multidisciplinary technology organization;

 Strengthen organizational capabilities across product management, software engineering, enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, data and AI, cloud and infrastructure, and technology operations;

 Foster a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, accountability, collaboration, security-by-design, and user-centred product development.

 Supervisory Responsibilities 
 Yes

 Salary Range 
 $230,000 to $250,000/year

 Position Type 
 Backfill

 Qualifications Expected for Position 
 Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Health Informatics, Business or related field (advanced degree preferred);

 12+ years of progressive senior leadership experience in technology, product management, digital transformation, and/or data and analytics, within healthcare, virtual/hybrid care, or a highly regulated sector;

 Demonstrated ability to develop and execute technology strategies that align with organizational objectives and deliver measurable business outcomes;

 Deep understanding of cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, cloud technologies, data and analytics, AI, and emerging technology trends;

 Demonstrated experience leading technology modernization, digital transformation, and enterprise technology operations;

 Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and change leadership skills, with the ability to collaborate with clinical, commercial, operations, legal, privacy, and compliance functions, and global counterparts;

 Demonstrated success leading multi-disciplinary, distributed, and high-performing teams within a complex, multinational corporate structure; and

 Strong strategic planning and execution capabilities, with a proven track record of managing technology portfolios, product roadmaps, budgets, vendors, and delivery outcomes.

 Work Environment 
 ☐ Office ☐ Remote ☒ Hybrid (Office & Remote)

 Travel: up to 10% 
 Travel percentage reflects an estimate and is subject to change dependent on business needs.

 Physical Requirements 
 To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential job duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions. Teladoc Health will make reasonable accommodations for the known
 physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified individual in line with company policy.

 About Us 
 Teladoc Health is the global virtual care leader, offering the only comprehensive virtual care solution spanning telehealth, expert medical, and licensed platform services. Teladoc Health serves the world's leading insurers, employers, and health systems and helps millions of people around the world resolve
 their healthcare needs with confidence.

 Job Description Acknowledgment 
 This job description is a general overview of the nature and level of work performed by employees with this job designation. It is not intended to be a comprehensive list of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of this position. Management reserves the right to add, delete, and/or modify any
 of the job duties or requirements at any time. I acknowledge that I have read and understand the above job description. By signing this job description, I understand the duties that are expected of me.

 Why Join Teladoc Health? 

 Impactful, Connected Healthcare: Support millions of Canadians across the country with accessible care within rural regions & provincial health systems, at no cost to patients. 

 Focus on Quality & Safety: Upholding the highest excellence of clinical quality standards is paramount to Teladoc Health. 

 Collaborative, Supportive Network: Our diverse community is dedicated to transforming healthcare in Canada. Be a part of a growing team across Canada, that thrives on engagement, learning and growth. 

 Our Work Truly Matters: Recognized as the world leader in whole-person virtual care, Teladoc Health uses innovative platforms to provide accessible care across the full continuum of care, at every stage in a person’s health journey. 

 Growth and Innovation: We are growing rapidly - Come grow with us and support our expanding mission to make healthcare more accessible. 

 Diversity and Inclusion: At Teladoc Health we believe that personal and professional diversity is the key to innovation. We hire based solely on your strengths and qualifications, and the way in which those strengths can directly contribute to your success in your new position. 

 Teladoc Health Canada, Inc. uses artificial intelligence-assisted tools as part of our recruitment process, including to screen and evaluate candidates. These tools support, but do not replace, human judgment. Our hiring team makes all final decisions.

 At Teladoc Health we thrive on difference and individuality. Teladoc Health is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. 

 We are committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment, where all employees and customers feel valued, respected and supported. We are dedicated to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of our customers and communities in which we live and serve. jobs.title: Director, Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
Join the team leading the next evolution of virtual care.  

 At Teladoc Health, you are empowered to bring your true self to work while helping millions of people live their healthiest lives.

 Here you will be part of a high-performance culture where colleagues embrace challenges, drive transformative solutions, and create opportunities for growth. Together, we’re transforming how better health happens.

 Position Summary 
 We are seeking a Director, Platform Engineering & DevOps to lead the development and maturation of our enterprise Platform Engineering organization.

 This leader will be responsible for building a modern, automation-first platform primarily focused on Microsoft Azure, while supporting remaining legacy workloads in AWS and on-premises data centers during the company's migration to Azure.

 The Director will lead the Platform Engineering team and partner closely with Network Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Security, and application Engineering to deliver secure, reliable, scalable, and highly automated infrastructure platforms.

 A key objective of this role is to move the organization toward a self-service Platform Engineering model, enabling application teams to deploy and manage infrastructure using standardized patterns, Infrastructure as Code, automation, and cloud governance.

 Role and Responsibilities 
 Build, lead, and develop the Platform Engineering organization, including engineering strategy, roadmap, standards, and operating model.
 Lead the design and evolution of the company's enterprise Microsoft Azure platform, including landing zones, governance, identity, networking, security, observability, and resiliency.

 Support the migration of applications and infrastructure from AWS and on-premises environments to Azure.

 Establish Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and automation as the standard approach for provisioning and managing infrastructure.

 Develop reusable Terraform modules, CI/CD pipelines, reference architectures, and standardized deployment patterns.

 Build self-service platform capabilities and "golden paths" that improve developer productivity and reduce manual infrastructure provisioning.

 Partner with Network Engineering on hybrid cloud connectivity, cloud networking, Private Link, DNS, routing, firewalls, and application delivery.

 Partner with SRE to establish platform availability objectives, observability standards, resiliency practices, incident improvements, and operational readiness, leveraging Datadog Application

 Partner with SRE and Application Engineering to establish consistent standards for application and platform telemetry, including metrics, logs, distributed traces, dashboards, alerting, and service-level monitoring.

 Ensure cloud and platform services are appropriately instrumented and integrated with the enterprise observability platform.

 Partner with Security to implement secure-by-default platform patterns, cloud governance, policy enforcement, and compliance controls.

 Establish cloud cost-management and FinOps practices across Azure and remaining AWS environments.

 Recruit, mentor, and develop engineering leaders and senior technical talent.

 Provide executive-level communication regarding platform strategy, technology risks, investments, reliability, and cloud transformation progress.

 Required Qualifications 
 10+ years of progressive experience in cloud infrastructure, DevOps, Platform Engineering, systems engineering, or related disciplines, including significant engineering leadership experience.

 Deep technical knowledge of Microsoft Azure, including enterprise cloud architecture, networking, security, governance, resiliency, and platform services.

 Strong experience with Infrastructure as Code and automation, particularly Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, and Git-based engineering workflows.

 Demonstrated experience leading complex cloud transformation initiatives, including hybrid environments, enterprise cloud migrations, or modernization of mission-critical infrastructure.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience building or leading an enterprise Platform Engineering organization or Internal Developer Platform.

 Working knowledge of AWS and experience supporting or migrating AWS workloads.

 Experience with Azure Landing Zones, Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework, Azure Well-Architected Framework, and Azure Verified Modules.

 Experience with Kubernetes and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).

 Experience with GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, GitHub Actions or comparable DevOps platforms.

 Experience with enterprise observability and APM platforms, preferably Datadog, and technologies such as OpenTelemetry.

 Experience implementing SRE practices including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, resiliency engineering, and incident management.

 Experience implementing cloud FinOps and cost optimization practices.

 Experience operating technology platforms in healthcare, SaaS, financial services, or another regulated environment.

 Success Metrics for the Role 
 Success will be measured by the Director's ability to build a scalable Platform Engineering organization and improve the speed, reliability, security, and efficiency of infrastructure delivery.
 Increased percentage of infrastructure deployed and managed through Infrastructure as Code.

 Increased adoption of standardized Azure landing zones, reusable platform services, and self-service capabilities.

 Reduced infrastructure provisioning and application deployment lead times.

 Progress migrating targeted AWS and on-premises workloads to Azure.

 Improved platform availability and achievement of defined SLOs.

 Increased adoption and effectiveness of standardized observability and APM practices across platform and application services, including improved service visibility and reduced mean time to detect and restore.

 Reduction in infrastructure-related incidents, configuration drift, and manual production changes.

 Improved developer satisfaction and adoption of Platform Engineering services.

 Improved cloud governance, security compliance, and cost efficiency.

 Successful recruitment, development, and retention of a high-performing Platform Engineering team.

 As part of our hiring process, we verify identity and credentials, conduct interviews (live or video), and screen for fraud or misrepresentation. Applicants who falsify information will be disqualified.

 Why join Teladoc Health? 

 Teladoc Health is transforming how better health happens. Learn how when you join us in pursuit of our impactful mission. 

 Chart your career path with meaningful opportunities that empower you to grow, lead, and make a difference.

 Join a multi-faceted community that celebrates each colleague’s unique perspective and is focused on continually improving, each and every day.  

 Contribute to an innovative culture where fresh ideas are valued as we increase access to care in new ways.   

 Enjoy an inclusive benefits program centered around you and your family, with tailored programs that address your unique needs.

 Explore candidate resources with tips and tricks from Teladoc Health recruiters and learn more about our company culture by exploring #TeamTeladocHealth on LinkedIn.

 As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we never have and never will discriminate against any job candidate or employee due to age, race, religion, color, ethnicity, national origin, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, membership in an employee organization, medical condition, family history, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, parental status, or pregnancy). In our innovative and inclusive workplace, we prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind. 

 Teladoc Health respects your privacy and is committed to maintaining the confidentiality and security of your personal information. In furtherance of your employment relationship with Teladoc Health, we collect personal information responsibly and in accordance with applicable data privacy laws, including but not limited to, the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).  Personal information is defined as: Any information or set of information relating to you, including (a) all information that identifies you or could reasonably be used to identify you, and (b) all information that any applicable law treats as personal information. jobs.description:
Who We Are 
 Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital agency and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture.
 With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across: Digital Product Strategy & Innovation, Digital Marketing Services, Web & Mobile App Development, Data & AI, Cloud Engineering, and Enterprise Technology Modernization.
 From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

 Location & Flexibility 
 Our Director & Practice Lead, Data Engineering will operate remotely in Canada OR be based out of either our Toronto, ON or Vancouver, BC office locations.

 The Opportunity 
 TELUS Digital's Data, AI & Cloud (DAIC) practice is the multidisciplinary engine behind enterprise AI, blending boutique innovation with the breadth of a global services portfolio to help organizations architect, scale, and secure their transformations. Spanning our full family of specialized capabilities, the DAIC practice delivers end-to-end solutions across AI Advisory, AI Solutions, Data & AI Platforms, and Cloud Transformation.
 As a premier Google Cloud partner, our Cloud practice is at the forefront of helping enterprises adopt and scale on Google Cloud infrastructure: delivering complex engineering, deployment, and migration programs for some of the largest organizations in Canada and beyond.

 Location & Flexibility 
 This role will operate remotely in the United States or Canada OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.
 This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

 This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

 This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.
 Responsibilities 
 Strategic Account Governance & Growth 
 Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).

 Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.

 Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.

 Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

 Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.

 Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.

 Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.

 Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.

 Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

 Leadership & Talent Development 
 Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.

 Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.

 Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

 Operational & Financial Stewardship 
 Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.

 Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.

 Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.

 Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

 Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.

 Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.

 Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.

 Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.

 Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.

 Align application release schedules with the financial close calendar, collaborating with Technology, Risk, and Internal Audit to enforce rigorous segregation of duties, access controls, and Internal Control over Financial Reporting (ICFR).
 Finance Data, BI & Analytics
 Direct the team responsible for designing, building, and operating finance data models, data pipelines, and certified financial data products on Snowflake, establishing a single source of truth across all global entities.
 Establish robust semantic layer governance, ensuring every certified data product possesses an assigned Finance owner, approved definitions, and ongoing reconciliation to general ledger accounting outputs.
 Oversee Finance’s enterprise Business Intelligence (BI) capabilities and visualization standards, transitioning teams from static reporting to dynamic, interactive dashboards and executive decision environments utilizing tools such as Amazon QuickSight and native cloud analytics capabilities.
 Accelerate data-driven insights across Finance by collaborating with Finance Business Partners and operational data teams to integrate financial and operational drivers, including trading, clearing, listings, and market data subscriptions.

 Monitor evolving capabilities across Workday, Snowflake, business intelligence ecosystems, and emerging financial technologies, assessing business viability and integrating high-value opportunities into the strategic roadmap.
 Provide strategic advisory to the Finance Senior Leadership Team on emerging technology trends, fostering shared ownership of digital adoption.
 People Leadership & Change Enablement
 Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team spanning finance systems, data engineering, business intelligence, and advanced analytics, establishing clear strategic direction while scaling functional capacity.
 Drive enterprise change management, communication, and training programs to embed digital literacy and analytical curiosity across the broader finance organization.
 Manage the Digital Finance operational budget, serving as the business partner to Technology and Procurement for vendor selection and delivery partner management.

 Must Have(s) 
 12+ years of progressive finance experience with comprehensive knowledge of core accounting and financial processes, coupled with advanced financial analysis capabilities.
 Professional accounting or financial credential (CPA preferred; MBA or CFA will also be considered).
 Demonstrated success serving as the business lead for major finance transformations (e.g., enterprise ERP implementations, EPM/planning platforms, or enterprise data and reporting overhauls) from conception through operational adoption and value realization.
 Proven leadership experience guiding data, BI, or analytics personnel, underpinned by sufficient technical literacy in data modeling, SQL, cloud data platforms (e.g., Snowflake), and modern BI suites to establish standards and guide technical execution.
 Deep knowledge of financial governance frameworks, internal controls, and ICFR requirements within large-scale system and process transformation environments.
 Demonstrated track record managing multi-year business cases, departmental budgets, third-party software vendors, and systems integration partners.
 Proven leadership acumen in ambiguous, matrixed environments with strong cross-functional stakeholder management and executive presentation skills.

 Nice to Have(s) 
 Experience with Workday Financials and Workday Adaptive Planning, including Foundation Data Model (FDM) architecture and data integration with Snowflake.
 Direct technical experience with data querying and scripting languages (e.g., SQL, Python).
 Practical experience deploying artificial intelligence or machine learning solutions within corporate finance environments, including model validation and risk management frameworks.
 Industry experience within capital markets, financial services, financial technology, or software organizations.
 Leadership background within multi-entity, multi-currency, and multinational operating structures.
 Experience building, structuring, and scaling a digital or transformation function from early-stage maturity.

 What Makes You a Great Fit 

 You take ownership and follow through

 You're comfortable solving problems and figuring things out

 You care about the team, not just your own work

 You bring a sense of humor and perspective to what you do

 About the Opportunity 

 We are seeking a hands-on Vice President, Financial Planning & Analysis to own enterprise-wide planning, forecasting, and performance analytics for a growth-stage SaaS business. This is not a purely oversight role, the VP, FP&A will be in the models directly, building and stress-testing scenarios, and translating the numbers into decisions. Reporting to the CFO, this person will be a key partner to executive leadership and business unit owners, and will play a central role in the company's next chapter of growth.

 We're looking for someone who wants to build, not just review, someone as comfortable inside the mechanics of a model as they are presenting its output to the CFO and board. 

 Key Responsibilities: 

 10+ years of progressive finance experience, including FP&A leadership, with a track record of being genuinely hands-on in the model — not several layers removed from it.

 Exposure to an exit, sale process, recapitalization, refinancing, or similar transaction, with a working understanding of what "diligence-ready" actually looks like.

 Executive presence — able to move fluidly between deep model work and clear, confident presentation to the CFO and board.

 Strong judgment about what's urgent, what's important, and what can wait — able to prioritize across competing asks from the CFO, business leaders, and the sponsor.

 Nice-to-haves:

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
JOB PURPOSE 
 Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization. 

 The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement. 

 KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals. 
 Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness. 
 Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options. 
 Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes. 
 Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks. 
 AI Solution Development & Implementation Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities. 
 Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working. 
 Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement. 
 Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured. 
 Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk. 
 AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption. 
 Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks. 
 Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements. 
 Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed. 
 Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required. 
 Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users. 
 Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI. 
 Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support. 
 Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement. 
 Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption 
 Vendor, Technology & Partner Management Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership. 
 Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization. 
 Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation. 
 Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value. 
 QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
  Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. 
 Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption. 
 Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization. 
 Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI. 
 Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance.
